requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute to MessagePack.Annotations, with an optional `SurrogateType` property. The source generator gains a new pipeline for classes carrying the attribute. `GeneratedFormatterCollector` checks the class: it must be partial, implement exactly one `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, and `T` must be a supported type. It then builds an `ObjectSerializationInfo` with `IsUserDeclaredFormatter = true`. The two formatter templates then emit `partial class <UserFormatter>` instead of `internal sealed class`. Without a surrogate, every public read-write instance member is serialized under its name as a string key. With a surrogate, the surrogate's `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` attributes decide keys and membership, and its members are matched to the target by name and type. The generator reports four new diagnostics, MsgPack019 to MsgPack022, and reuses MsgPack004, 005, 007 and 008-style ids. User-declared formatters are excluded from the hand-written custom formatter list so they are not registered twice. A new ExternalTypes test project (no MessagePack reference) plus execution and generator diagnostic tests come with the change, along with README and analyzer docs.
story.why: REQ-2129 asks to generate a formatter in Project B for a type defined in Project A, which cannot reference MessagePack. The trigger is a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute on a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`. The requirement lists three options for supplying key metadata. The agent picked none of them. It invented a fourth design: a contractless default plus a compile-time surrogate type.

findings.description: Claim C6 disputed: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L54-56 checks i.IsGenericType && Equals(i.OriginalDefinition, openFormatterInterface), which matches open constructed interfaces too (for example partial class MyFormatter<T> : IMessagePackFormatter<T> has formatterInterfaces.Length == 1 and fails later at L64 with MsgPack021, not MsgPack020). Also, FormatterMustImplementFormatterOfT (GeneratedMessagePackFormatterTests.cs L57-75) only tests zero interfaces, never multiple IMessagePackFormatter<T> interfaces.

Claim C9 disputed: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L84-85 does NOT set cast flags for explicit interface implementations: in Roslyn C#, when m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations.Length > 0, m.Name is the interface-qualified name (such as MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize), never OnBeforeSerialize or OnAfterDeserialize, so needsCast is always false. Moreover, [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] can target types in assemblies that do reference MessagePack (including the current compilation), where an explicit implementation will emit uncast calls that fail to compile.

Claim C10 disputed: First, citation GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L87-102 over-cites L94-97 (the else branch calling CreateSurrogateMembers), which neither C10 nor any other claim describes. Second, IsPublicReadWrite at L279-281 also includes public init-only ({ get; init; }) properties because SetMethod.DeclaredAccessibility is Public even when IsInitOnly is true. Third, none of the three named tests cover fields, base-type member inheritance/shadowing, or indexers.

Claim C14 disputed: Neither named test (SurrogateKeysMustNotMixStringAndInt, SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership) tests reporting MemberNeedsKey at GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L171-179. Also, member discovery relies on GetInstanceMembers (L249-275, uncited by C14), which inspects only non-implicitly-declared, non-indexer fields and properties rather than all instance members, and the quoted requirement's 'other settings (such as Union)' is not supported.

Claim C16 disputed: The sole named test SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership (GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests.cs L55-69) only tests integer surrogate keys (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L206-207); the string-key surrogate path at L208 (and keyKindIsInt == false at L211) as well as IsInitOnly (L219) and IsRequired (L220-225) are not tested by it or any other test in the diff.

Claim C18 disputed: Citation GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypes.cs L1-50 is over-cited: lines 24-37 define ExternalWidgetSurrogate and lines 39-50 define the [MessagePackObject] class ContainsExternalPerson, neither of which C18 describes.

Claim C26 disputed: doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md L26 states 'Any nesting types that contain the formatter must also be declared partial', but GeneratedFormatterCollector.IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L293-299) never checks containing types, so MsgPack019 is not reported when an enclosing type lacks partial. Additionally, README.md L1655 and doc/analyzers/MsgPack022.md L3 state only read-write members are matched, whereas IsPublicReadWrite (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L279-281) also matches public init-only properties.

IsPartial checks only the formatter class, not its containing types. The MsgPack019 doc (line 26) says nesting types must also be partial. A formatter nested in a non-partial class passes the check, and the generated `partial class Outer` wrapper then fails with a raw compiler error instead of MsgPack019.

Every surrogate instance member without `[IgnoreMember]` must carry a `[Key]`, including private fields and members inherited from surrogate base types. Missing keys raise MemberNeedsKey and abort generation. The attribute XML doc says only `[Key]`-carrying members are matched, and the README says only the members the surrogate lists are serialized. Both suggest unkeyed members are simply ignored.

The new project targets only net8.0, yet ExecutionTests references it. If ExecutionTests multi-targets an older framework such as net472 or net6.0, the ProjectReference cannot be resolved for that target and the build breaks.

Attributed formatters are removed from the custom-formatter list. Other generator checks that use this list to decide whether a member type such as ExternalPerson is formattable may then treat it as unknown. Only one execution test (MessagePackObjectCanContainExternalTypes) covers this, and no diagnostic test does.

The predicate accepts only ClassDeclarationSyntax, while the attribute's AttributeTargets.Class also allows `record` classes. A `partial record` marked with the attribute is silently ignored, with no diagnostic and no generated formatter.

The diagnostics pipeline combines symbol-holding requests with CompilationProvider. Collect then runs twice per formatter on every compilation change. Holding symbols and Locations in the incremental pipeline defeats caching. Existing pipelines also hold symbols, so this is an IDE performance risk rather than a correctness bug.

Several paths have no test: the body-less `partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` form the issue explicitly mentions, duplicate surrogate keys, unkeyed surrogate members, NoDeserializingConstructor, and generic, inaccessible or enum data types.

GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect never validates the formatter class's own modifiers, arity, or resolver accessibility. Declaring a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class as abstract, generic (or nested in a generic type), file-local, or private/protected inside an outer class passes all checks in Collect and emits uncompilable source in GeneratedMessagePackResolver (CS0144, CS0122, CS9054, or unbound type parameters) with no analyzer/generator diagnostic. Similarly, L66 checks IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter) rather than accessibility from GeneratedMessagePackResolver, so a private nested target type inside the same outer class also fails to compile in GeneratedMessagePackResolver (CS0122/CS0051).

Invalid or open SurrogateType arguments silently produce wrong formatters with zero diagnostics: (1) casting NamedArguments SurrogateType via 'as INamedTypeSymbol' turns non-named types such as typeof(MyType[]) into null, causing Collect to silently fall back to contractless string-key serialization instead of reporting an error; (2) passing an unbound generic typeof(MySurrogate<>) or an enum produces an INamedTypeSymbol whose GetInstanceMembers(surrogate) is empty, silently generating a formatter that serializes 0 members ({}) and discards all data.

Callback-receiver explicit-implementation detection is broken: in Roslyn C#, an explicit interface implementation's IMethodSymbol.Name includes the interface prefix (e.g. 'MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize'), never 'OnBeforeSerialize' or 'OnAfterDeserialize' (which is on m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations[0].Name), and type.GetMembers() misses base-type implementations. Consequently needsCast is always false, and any formatted type that explicitly implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver generates uncast calls that fail to compile with CS1061.

IsPartial only checks whether formatter itself has the partial keyword and does not walk formatter.ContainingType. If a partial [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class is nested inside a non-partial class or struct, MsgPack019 is not reported and EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces emits a partial declaration for the outer type, failing compilation with CS0260.

CreateSurrogateMembers checks 'if (key is not (int or string))' without rejecting negative integer keys (intKey < 0). A surrogate member annotated with [Key(-1)] passes validation and feeds a negative key into FormatterTemplate, producing broken or uncompilable generated formatter code.

Deserialization always emits 'new T()' with only the collected members and no constructor arguments, without checking whether the target type declares C# 'required' members that were excluded (either omitted/[IgnoreMember]-ed by a surrogate or skipped in contractless mode due to a non-public getter). When any excluded member is required, generated code fails to compile with CS9035.

GeneratedFormatterCollector ignores [ExcludeFormatterFromSourceGeneratedResolver] and performs no duplicate-target check when multiple [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes format the same type T (e.g., with different surrogates) or format a type already marked [MessagePackObject], leading either to silent dropping of one formatter's body in ImmutableSortedSet<ObjectSerializationInfo> (CS0535) or duplicate registrations in GeneratedMessagePackResolver.

Surrogate diagnostics at L175, L185, L194, and L201 use 'surrogateMember.Locations.FirstOrDefault() ?? location'. If the surrogate type lives in a referenced assembly, Locations contains a non-null MetadataLocation (IsInSource == false), preventing fallback to the formatter's source location and emitting diagnostics without a source file/line.
